observation_summary: The Fraction and BigFraction constructors throw a FractionConversionException when converting a double value to a fraction if the denominator exceeds the overflow limit, even when the current approximation is already sufficiently accurate and within the specified maxDenominator.
hypothesis: The logic for throwing an overflow exception is too aggressive. It fails to check if the current approximation (p1/q1) is already valid and within the maxDenominator limit before throwing an exception when the next iteration (p2/q2) overflows.
prediction: Adding a check to verify if the previous denominator (q1) is within the maxDenominator limit when epsilon is zero will allow the algorithm to terminate gracefully by returning the last valid fraction instead of throwing an exception.
experiment_rationale: The fix introduces a conditional check (if epsilon == 0.0 && FastMath.abs(q1) < maxDenominator) before the exception is thrown. This confirms that the root cause was a missing validation check for the state of the previous iteration.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by a missing guard condition. The code was unconditionally throwing an exception when the next iteration's denominator overflowed, without checking if the current (already calculated) fraction was sufficient. Adding this check resolves the issue, making it a classic 'Checking' defect.
evidence_used: The fix adds an 'if' condition before the 'throw new FractionConversionException' statement.
The condition checks if the previous denominator (q1) is within the allowed maxDenominator.
The bug report states that the exception is thrown even when the value is very close to a simple fraction.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the flow, the root cause is the absence of a validation check (guard) to handle the edge case where the current approximation is already valid.
